question: A network administrator must create a Linux container on a Cisco Nexus Series Switch. The container requires 10 percent of the CPU of the switch and 1024 MB of RAM to run successfully. Which task provides the necessary resources?
options: Edit the container properties with the guestshell run command.
Increase the compute resources with the guestshell resize command.
Modify resource allocation with the virtual-service resize command.
Enable the Bash shell of the switch with the feature bash command.
theory: Guest Shell starts with modest default CPU/memory/rootfs limits; the documented way to raise them is the 'guestshell resize {cpu | memory | rootfs}' command (e.g., resizing memory to 1024 MB and CPU to 10%), followed by a Guest Shell reboot to apply the new limits before installing a heavier container workload. There is no 'virtual-service resize' or 'guestshell run' command, and enabling the separate Bash shell feature does nothing to a Guest Shell container's resource allocation. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 16 — Automation and Scripting Tools)
